title: r/longevity on Reddit: Forever Healthy's Risk Benefit Analysis of Fisetin as a Senolytic Therapy
abstract:
But senolytics are probably just attacking ONE symptom of aging anyway. We need something more profound. No need to take any risks now, unless you are already suffering severe aging effects. ... I agree about synolytics attacking just one aspect of ageing but it's a pretty important one that looks "easy" to treat compared to the other causes of ageing. From my experience with Dasatinib one dose a year or so should be enough. If you take it Fisetin all the time and you see nothing it may not be doing anything.
195K subscribers in the longevity community. Reasons to hope to see the age of 100 and beyond: Biomedical rejuvenation through damage repair, manipulation of metabolism, beyond the mere results of exercise, caloric restriction, and fasting. Stem cell therapies, anti-cancer viruses, gene therapy, senolytics, and whatever is coming next...

They want to know exactly what the benefit is in humans, make sure that the dose is correctly formulated (i.e. don't want to use some product that is part fisetin and part something else that might interfere), or if there's no benefit wait until a good senolytic is demonstrated for use in humans.
